name: Pediatric-inspired multi-agent regimen for AYA adult ALL (CALGB 10403-type)
disease: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, adolescent and young adult (AYA)
histology: B-lineage or T-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia

biomarkers.note: Pediatric-inspired regimens are the preferred approach for Philadelphia chromosome-negative AYA ALL; BCR::ABL1-positive disease is routed to a TKI-containing protocol (see heme-all-ph-positive-tki). BCR::ABL1 is tested to establish the gate. Harrison 22nd ed. Table 111-4 (line 120095) lists a pediatric-inspired approach with few/no stem-cell transplant for B-lineage Ph-negative AYA (15 to 35/45 years).

treatmentSetting: induction, consolidation, interim maintenance, delayed intensification, and maintenance

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adolescent / young adult (AYA), approximately 15 to 39 years

drugs.name: vinCRIStine
drugs.notes: Induction backbone drug. Harrison line 120175 states ALL induction regimens are centered around vincristine, glucocorticoids, and anthracyclines. Adult AYA CALGB 10403-type mg/m2 doses and days are not printed in the adult ALL extracts - dose, unit, basis, and days are VERIFY (pediatric-guideline values are reference-only and not adopted as the adult dose). Per-dose cap 2 mg applied as a StewardMD safety rule; ISMP tall-man vinCRIStine, IV-only, fatal if intrathecal.

drugs.name: Glucocorticoid (prednisone or dexamethasone)
drugs.notes: Induction backbone glucocorticoid (Harrison line 120175). Dexamethasone penetrates the blood-brain barrier and is often preferred (Harrison line 120175). Adult AYA mg dose and schedule not printed in the adult ALL extracts - dose, unit, basis, and days are VERIFY.

drugs.name: Anthracycline (DAUNOrubicin or DOXOrubicin)
drugs.notes: Induction backbone anthracycline (Harrison line 120175 names anthracyclines; Fig 111-1 abbreviations list daunorubicin/doxorubicin). Adult AYA mg/m2 dose and days not printed - dose, unit, basis, and days are VERIFY. Cumulative-lifetime cap (warn 450 / hard 550 mg/m2 doxorubicin-equivalent) applied as a StewardMD safety rule; verify institutional daunorubicin-to-doxorubicin conversion.

drugs.name: Asparaginase (pegaspargase / L-asparaginase)
drugs.notes: The pediatric-inspired signature drug. Harrison line 120177 states L-asparaginase is the only ALL-specific drug and is now more intensively used in adults, with pegylated asparaginase giving longer asparagine depletion. Adult AYA dose (units or units/m2) and schedule not printed in the adult ALL extracts - dose, unit, basis, and days are VERIFY. Monitor for thrombosis (consider antithrombin/anticoagulation), pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, hyperglycemia, and hypersensitivity; Erwinia asparaginase is the substitute after hypersensitivity.

drugs.name: Intrathecal CNS prophylaxis (methotrexate +/- cytarabine)
drugs.notes: MANDATORY CNS prophylaxis (Harrison lines 120134 to 120138: intrathecal methotrexate alone or with cytarabine, with or without a glucocorticoid). Intrathecal agents are cytarabine and methotrexate ONLY; vinCRIStine must NEVER be given intrathecally. Fixed doses not printed - VERIFY.

supportiveCare: tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis (hydration, allopurinol or rasburicase, electrolyte monitoring) - Harrison line 120030
asparaginase toxicity surveillance: thrombosis, pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, hyperglycemia, hypersensitivity
high-dose methotrexate phases (if used): mandatory leucovorin rescue plus methotrexate-level monitoring
maintenance phase is 6-mercaptopurine plus methotrexate plus intrathecal therapy, approximately 2 to 2.5 years (Harrison lines 120044 to 120047)
antiemetic and growth-factor support per NCCN tiers (pending per-disease template)

monitoring: CBC with differential before each phase and during aplasia
coagulation / fibrinogen and thrombosis surveillance during asparaginase
hepatic and renal function; methotrexate levels during high-dose methotrexate phases
cardiac assessment and cumulative anthracycline tracking

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

core.locator: lines 120044 to 120047 (maintenance 6-MP + MTX + intrathecal), 120095 (Table 111-4 pediatric-inspired AYA), 120175 to 120177 (induction identity: vincristine, glucocorticoids, anthracyclines, L-asparaginase), 120134 to 120138 (intrathecal CNS prophylaxis)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric ALL extract (reference only; pediatric-inspired identity, not adopted as adult doses)
guideline.locator: guidelines/ped_all.txt (pediatric COG-type induction with vincristine, glucocorticoid, anthracycline, and pegaspargase; adult AYA regimens such as CALGB 10403 are patterned on this pediatric backbone)

provenanceNote: Textbook-grounded StewardMD draft for AYA adult ALL. The pediatric-inspired identity (vincristine/glucocorticoid/anthracycline/asparaginase induction backbone with intrathecal CNS prophylaxis and prolonged 6-MP/methotrexate maintenance), its AYA setting, and its Philadelphia-negative gate are grounded in Harrison 22nd ed. Chapter 111 (Table 111-4 line 120095 and the induction/maintenance text). Adult AYA CALGB 10403-type per-drug doses and phase/cycle structure are NOT printed in the available adult ALL extracts and are left VERIFY rather than borrowed from the pediatric guideline; the vincristine 2 mg per-dose cap and anthracycline cumulative cap are applied as StewardMD safety rules. NCCN per-disease template, StewardMD clinical (R1) review, and any hospital-implementation overlay approval are pending. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
